title: GROUPBY and PIVOTBY hold an array returned by their LAMBDA inside its cell; INDEX boxes it unless computed, and N(boxed) is #VALUE!
statement: Measured in Excel 16.0.20527 through COM (dc-h9u), when a GROUPBY or PIVOTBY callback LAMBDA returns an array, Excel keeps that array held inside its result cell rather than flattening or failing immediately: a cell spilling that held array shows #VALUE!, an operator over the result is #VALUE! in a dynamic-array formula (and takes the first element in a legacy formula), SUM/COUNT/COUNTA read across its elements, and MAX/MIN/AVERAGE/PRODUCT/SUMSQ give #N/A. INDEX(GROUPBY(...), 1, 2) returns a boxed array that displays its first element (so *10 multiplies the first element and TYPE gives 1, while SUM/ROWS/CONCAT read the whole array); however N(INDEX(GROUPBY(...), 1, 2)) returns #VALUE!, and omitting the column selector as INDEX(INDEX(GROUPBY(...), 0, 2), 1) leaves the inner array held (#VALUE!). When the group LAMBDA builds a computed array (for example LAMBDA(x, x+0), TRANSPOSE(x), or FILTER(x, x>0)), INDEX(GROUPBY(...), 1, 2) spills that array in a dynamic-array formula. In PIVOTBY with several value columns and one function, Total and column subtotal columns are blank; with several functions they carry values.
basis: Read from Excel 16.0.20527 COM measurements recorded in DnaCalc commits ad40ea44 (about 160 dynamic-array and legacy grouping formulas), a61f6695 (15 PIVOTBY multi-field depth calls), d96d8cba (held_arrays explicit dynamic-formula tests), and 2,055 grouping rows in catalogue sheet dch9u_functions.
